A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLM-Streamline despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments on Llama2 and OPT models, including benchmark results and replacement-network and training-data ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original pruning results, stability measurements, architecture and initialization analyses, and comparisons of layer replacement with LoRA, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The core procedure remains cosine-based selection of consecutive layers followed by learned replacement. v3 adds SwiGLU as a replacement architecture. Renaming MLP to FFN and explicitly specifying MSE training do not establish changes to the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The stated data source for the layer-redundancy probe changes from WikiText-2 in v1 Section 3.2 to multi-domain SlimPajama samples in v3 Sections 2.1 and 4.1. Benchmark coverage otherwise remains: the 12 classification and three generation benchmarks are retained, and the six smaller-OPT benchmarks move to Appendix C.1.

E2.justification: v3 adds SliceGPT comparisons on OPT-6.7B, LLM-Pruner/SliceGPT participation on GSM8K and StrategyQA, TinyLlama/OpenLlama reference models, and a dedicated Llama2-7B LoRA comparison. The separate ShortGPT and ShortGPT* results are replaced by Ours(None), which v3 presents as covering ShortGPT/UIDL rather than reporting separate evaluations of them.

E3.justification: Reported replacement training changes from 20,000/10,000 samples for Llama2-7B/OPT-6.7B to 30,000 each, and from five epochs with batch size 2048 to 20 epochs with batch size 32. Main pruning ratios also change. v3 introduces stability evaluation and additional initialization, width, pruning-ratio, and LoRA protocols; these reported changes do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v1's training-data-size, parameter-sharing, and single-versus-multiple-MLP analyses disappear. v3 adds correctness-transition analysis, Llama2 replacement-width and initialization tests, validation-loss curves, Llama2 pruning-ratio comparisons, and explicit LoRA performance/memory analysis. The smaller-OPT pruning-ratio results remain in Appendix C.1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's PPL standard deviations measure dispersion across answer choices for its stability metric, rather than uncertainty in experimental results across runs.

E6.justification: v1 reports Llama2-7B MLP classification/generation averages of 45.2/21.7; v3 reports 45.8/22.4 for FFN and 45.2/24.7 for Layer under revised settings. These are not controlled version-to-version gains. v3 also adds stability, memory, and other analysis results, and changes retained summaries, including the highest-pruning OPT-2.7B average from 41.9 to 42.3.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3 introduces a formal confidence-weighted stability metric and supporting correctness-transition definitions, absent from v1. Equation 3 also resolves v1 Equation 5's argmin inconsistency by using argmax, agreeing with the maximum-similarity selection already shown in v1 Figure 1.

C1.justification: v3 makes stability a central contribution and claims superiority in both accuracy and stability. The headline retention claim changes from approximately 92% classification and 68% generation performance to 93% and 77% with 30,000 samples, while broadening v1's emphasis on a single MLP to alternative replacement networks.

C2.justification: v3 introduces the interpretation that accuracy can reward uncertain guesses, explains replacement's resource advantages over PEFT, and argues that transformer replacements could improve with further training. It removes v1's explicit scaling-law and generation-loss limitations, while adding narrower observations about GSM8K failures and training-cost tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies MSE fitting, 500 calibration samples, replacement initialization options, weight decay, LoRA rank 384, and separate post-training schedules and resource requirements. Appendix B substantially expands these details, but v1's smaller-OPT training configuration and WikiText-2/Alpaca post-training descriptions are no longer documented.

R1.justification: v3 adds UIDL, QLoRA, and Evaluating Quantized Large Language Models, and explicitly distinguishes its replacement stage from concurrent ShortGPT/UIDL work. It removes the separate distillation discussion and several low-rank and dataset references, while retaining the broad positioning within structured model pruning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves after experiments, a new metrics section is inserted, analysis is integrated into the experimental section, and detailed results are organized into a new Appendix C. The title and terminology also change.

P2.justification: The workflow diagram is redrawn and combined with a performance bar chart on the first page. The similarity plot is reformatted and relocated; confusion-category tables, stability tables, loss curves, pruning-ratio plots, and a memory comparison are added. Smaller-OPT results are consolidated in the appendix, alongside detailed new tables.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful architecture, pruning-ratio, and LoRA-memory analyses, clarifies training details, and resolves the pruning-selector inconsistency. However, it removes earlier ablations and explicit limitations, while its new central stability metric counts jointly incorrect predictions as stable even when their selected answers differ (Section 3, Equation 6). These gains and material concerns about evidence and interpretation leave the net overall quality change uncertain.
